needs_topo.message:
{function}() requires hy_topo.
  Current input is: {current}.
  Use add_toids() to build toid from fromnode/tonode, or hy(x, add_topo = TRUE).
needs_topo.message_python: {function}() needs toid, each flowline's downstream flowline, and the network (representation {current}) has neither toid nor the fromnode/tonode identifiers to build it from. All rows are affected. Add a toid column and call again.

placeholders.current: the representation of the input, as hy_network_type() returns it in R and representation() in Python

needs_topo.condition: The function needs each flowline's downstream flowline (toid), and the network has neither toid nor fromnode/tonode, the identifiers of the points at each end of every flowline that add_toids() builds toid from; the representation is then hy. Where the network has fromnode/tonode, the functions convert it themselves, except check_hy_graph() in R, which stops here with representation hy_node; add_toids() fixes that case. Where the downstream column has a source name the vocabulary lacks, registering it as toid (hydroloom_names() in R, register_names() in Python) is the alternative.
needs_topo.fix: Add a toid column giving each flowline's downstream flowline, then call again.
r_text:
<fn>() requires hy_topo.
  Current input is: <type>.
  Use add_toids() to build toid from fromnode/tonode, or hy(x, add_topo = TRUE).
check_hy_graph requires toid. Use add_toids() to build toid from fromnode/tonode, or hy(x, add_topo = TRUE).

needs_node.message:
{function}() requires hy_node.
  Current input is: {current}.
  Supply data with fromnode/tonode columns, or use make_node_topology() to build them.
needs_node.message_python: {function}() builds toid from fromnode and tonode, the identifiers of the points at each end of every flowline; the network (representation {current}) has no such columns, or an id repeats on more than one row. All rows are affected, or for a repeated id the rows sharing it. Add fromnode and tonode from the source data, or remove the duplicated rows, and call again.

placeholders.current: the representation of the input, as hy_network_type() returns it in R and representation() in Python

needs_node.condition: add_toids() builds each flowline's downstream flowline (toid) from the identifiers of the points at its upstream and downstream ends (fromnode, tonode). The network has no toid (with toid the stop is toid_already_present) and either lacks those columns or gives one flowline more than one row. make_node_topology() does not help here, since it builds fromnode/tonode from toid. Where an id repeats, removing the duplicated rows is the fix.
needs_node.rows: all; for a repeated id, the rows sharing it
needs_node.fix: Add fromnode and tonode columns from the source data, then call again.
r_text:
add_toids() requires hy_node.
  Current input is: <type>.
  Supply data with fromnode/tonode columns, or use make_node_topology() to build them.

toid_already_present.message: This network already has toid (class: {current}). add_toids() converts fromnode/tonode to toid.
toid_already_present.message_python: This network already gives each flowline its downstream flowline in toid (representation {current}); add_toids() only builds toid from fromnode/tonode. Use the network as it is, without add_toids().

placeholders.current: the representation of the input, as hy_network_type() returns it in R and representation() in Python

toid_already_present.condition: The network already gives each flowline its downstream flowline in toid; add_toids only builds toid from fromnode/tonode.
toid_already_present.fix: None needed: use the network as it is, without add_toids().
r_text: This network already has toid (class: <type>). add_toids() converts fromnode/tonode to toid.
network already contains a toid attribute

divergence_required.message: To remove non dendritic paths, a divergence attribute is required.
divergence_required.condition: Keeping only the main path where a flowline splits into two or more downstream flowlines (a divergence) needs the divergence column, which marks the main path 1 and minor paths 2; the network has none. To keep every path instead, to_flownetwork() needs no divergence.
divergence_required.fix: add_divergence(), given the coastal and inland outlets, to compute divergence.
r_text: To remove non dendritic paths, a divergence attribute is required.

return_dendritic_deprecated.message: return_dendritic = FALSE is deprecated. Use to_flownetwork() for non-dendritic edge lists.
return_dendritic_deprecated.message_python: add_toids() with return_dendritic false is deprecated: it keeps every downstream connection where a flowline splits into two or more downstream flowlines (a divergence). Call to_flownetwork() instead, which keeps both the main and minor paths.
return_dendritic_deprecated.condition: Keeping every downstream connection at a divergence by calling add_toids() with return_dendritic false is deprecated.
return_dendritic_deprecated.fix: to_flownetwork(), which keeps both the main and minor paths.
r_text: return_dendritic = FALSE is deprecated. Use to_flownetwork() for non-dendritic edge lists.

network_cycle.message: Some flowlines drain back into themselves: following toid downstream returns to the flowline it started from (a cycle). Run check_hy_graph() to list them, then correct their toid.
network_cycle.condition: Some flowlines drain back into themselves: following toid downstream from one of them returns to it, so the network has no upstream-to-downstream order.
network_cycle.rows: the flowlines in each cycle, as check_hy_graph() returns them
network_cycle.fix: check_hy_graph() to list them, then correct their toid.
r_text: Some flowlines drain back into themselves: following toid downstream returns to the flowline it started from (a cycle). Run check_hy_graph() to list them, then correct their toid.

id_toid_type_mismatch.message: id and toid have incompatible types (one character, one not). Outlet detection may be unreliable.
id_toid_type_mismatch.condition: One of id and toid is text and the other is not, so a toid can fail to match the id it points to and a flowline can be taken for an outlet, the flowline where water leaves the network.
id_toid_type_mismatch.fix: Convert id and toid to one type, for example text on both.
r_text: id and toid have incompatible types (one character, one not). Outlet detection may be unreliable.

outlet_fill_type_mismatch.message: Outlets cannot be marked: id is {id_type} and toid is {toid_type}, so the outlet value ("" where id is text, 0 otherwise) cannot be written into the rows with a missing toid. Convert id and toid to one type and call again.
outlet_fill_type_mismatch.condition: A missing toid marks an outlet and is filled with the reserved outlet value, which takes the type of id: "" where id is text, 0 otherwise. toid has a type that value cannot be written into.
outlet_fill_type_mismatch.rows: the rows with a missing toid
outlet_fill_type_mismatch.fix: Convert id and toid to one type before the call.
r_text: Can't convert `replace` <double> to match type of `data` <character>.

no_outlet.message: no outlets detected in network -- sort may produce incomplete results. A future release will treat this as an error.
no_outlet.condition: No flowline's toid leaves the network, so no flowline is an outlet (the flowline where water leaves the network) and the sort has nowhere to start. Such a network contains a cycle, and the flowlines in it and those draining into it are left out of the sort.
no_outlet.fix: check_hy_graph() to list the flowlines in the cycle; then give the outlet flowline a toid that is not an id.
r_text: no outlets detected in network -- sort may produce incomplete results. A future release will treat this as an error.

sort_missed_features.message: some features missed in sort. Are there loops in the network?
sort_missed_features.condition: Some flowlines were not reached from any outlet, usually because they drain into a cycle, a run of flowlines whose toid leads back to themselves; they and the cycle are left out of the result.
sort_missed_features.rows: the flowlines missing from the result
r_text: some features missed in sort. Are there loops in the network?

sort_runaway.message: runaway while loop, something wrong with the network?
sort_runaway.condition: The sort took more than twice as many steps as there are flowlines, which a cycle causes.
r_text: runaway while loop, something wrong with the network?

split_outlets_overlap.message: Are two or more outlets within the same network?
split_outlets_overlap.condition: With split true, each of the flowlines given in outlets, where each sorted group ends, gets its own group of upstream flowlines. One of the outlets passed is upstream of another, so the flowlines above the upstream one would belong to both groups. Sorting with split false, one group for the whole network, is the alternative.
split_outlets_overlap.rows: the flowlines reached from both outlets
split_outlets_overlap.fix: Remove the upstream one of the two from outlets, then call again.
r_text: Are two or more outlets within the same network?

index_mode_invalid.message: mode must be one of 'to', 'from', or 'both'.
index_mode_invalid.condition: mode is not recognized: "to" lists each flowline's downstream flowlines, "from" its upstream flowlines, "both" gives both.
index_mode_invalid.fix: Pass one of the three values.
r_text: mode must be one of 'to', 'from', or 'both'.

long_form_deprecated.message: long_form is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
long_form_deprecated.condition: The long table output of make_index_ids is deprecated.
long_form_deprecated.fix: Drop long_form. The default output's to_list table holds the same id, indid, and toindid, with one row per flowline and toindid a list of the downstream positions in place of one row per connection.
r_text: long_form is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

index_ids_direction_mismatch.message: Direction must be '{needed}' if x contains {mode} index ids
index_ids_direction_mismatch.message_python: This index was built with mode '{mode}' and can be walked only with direction '{needed}'. Build it again with make_index_ids() in the mode that matches the direction: 'to' for down or downmain, 'from' for up or upmain.

placeholders.needed: the direction the index supports, 'down' or 'up'
placeholders.mode: the mode the index was built with, 'to' or 'from'

index_ids_direction_mismatch.condition: An index built for downstream navigation (mode "to") cannot be walked upstream, nor one built for upstream navigation (mode "from") downstream.
index_ids_direction_mismatch.fix: make_index_ids() with mode "from" for up or upmain, "to" for down or downmain.
r_text: Direction must be 'down' if x contains to index ids
Direction must be 'up' if x contains from index ids

index_ids_missing_main.message: for {direction}, index ids must include main element
index_ids_missing_main.condition: The index carries no main-path flags (main), which upmain and downmain navigation follow at each divergence and confluence. make_index_ids() carries them only from the upmain/downmain columns, which to_flownetwork() sets from levelpath.
index_ids_missing_main.fix: add_levelpaths(), then to_flownetwork(), then make_index_ids() on the result.
r_text: for downmain, index ids must include main element
for upmain, index ids must include main element

network_not_frame_or_index_ids.condition: The input is neither a network table nor an index from make_index_ids(), so there is nothing to navigate.
network_not_frame_or_index_ids.fix: Pass the network table or make_index_ids() output.

main_path_required.message: main path must be provided for {direction} navigation
main_path_required.condition: upmain and downmain navigation follow the main path at each divergence and confluence; the network has no upmain/downmain columns to say which flowline that is.
main_path_required.fix: add_levelpaths(), then to_flownetwork(), which sets upmain and downmain from levelpath.
r_text: main path must be provided for downmain navigation

start_not_in_network.message: all starts must be in x
start_not_in_network.message_python: Every start must be an id in the network; one or more starts is missing or is not an id. Pass values of id as starts.
start_not_in_network.condition: A start is missing or is not an id in the network.
start_not_in_network.fix: Pass values of id as starts.
r_text: all starts must be in x

direction_invalid.message: direction '{direction}' is not one of the four navigation directions. Pass 'down', 'up', 'downmain', or 'upmain'.
direction_invalid.condition: direction is not one of down, up, downmain, upmain.

node_to_flownetwork_no_main.message: converting hy_node to non-dendritic edge list; upmain/downmain will not be set. Add divergence and levelpath attributes (see add_divergence(), add_levelpaths()) to preserve main-path information.
node_to_flownetwork_no_main.condition: fromnode/tonode alone do not say which flowline is the main path at a divergence or confluence, so the converted network carries no upmain/downmain.
node_to_flownetwork_no_main.fix: add_divergence(), given the coastal and inland outlets, then add_levelpaths(), before the conversion.
r_text: converting hy_node to non-dendritic edge list; upmain/downmain will not be set. Add divergence and levelpath attributes (see add_divergence(), add_levelpaths()) to preserve main-path information.

divergence_check_missing_columns.condition: The divergence check groups flowlines by the point where they begin (fromnode), which the flowlines leaving a divergence share, and reads which path is main (divergence); one or both columns are absent. Where fromnode is absent, make_node_topology() builds it from toid.
divergence_check_missing_columns.fix: add_divergence(), given the coastal and inland outlets, for divergence.
r_text: check_hy_graph: divergence_check requires attributes: <columns>

name_alias_conflict.message: Problem aligning names. {columns} conflicts with hydroloom name {names} can't proceed converting to hy object.
name_alias_conflict.message_python: Column {columns} would be renamed to the hydroloom name {names}, which another column already has, so two columns would carry one name. Drop or rename one of the two columns and call again.

placeholders.columns: the input columns that rename to a name already present, comma separated
placeholders.names: the hydroloom names they would take, comma separated

name_alias_conflict.condition: An input column renames to a hydroloom name that another column already has, so two columns would carry one name.
name_alias_conflict.rows: none; the columns are named in the message
name_alias_conflict.fix: Drop or rename one of the two columns.
r_text: Problem aligning names. <input columns> conflicts with hydroloom name <hydroloom names> can't proceed converting to hy object.

name_alias_duplicate.message:
Duplicate names found when aligning with hydroloom conventions 
 using {alias} from {aliases}

placeholders.alias: the input column that took the hydroloom name
placeholders.aliases: every input column that aliases that name, comma separated

name_alias_duplicate.condition: Two input columns are aliases of one hydroloom name. The one later in the alias list (a registered alias comes after the vocabulary's) took the name, and the message gives it after "using"; the other column kept its input name. Registering the intended mapping (hydroloom_names() in R, register_names() in Python) is the alternative to dropping a column.
name_alias_duplicate.rows: none; the columns are named in the message
name_alias_duplicate.fix: Drop the column that should not carry the hydroloom name.
r_text:
Duplicate names found when aligning with hydroloom conventions 
 using <alias> from <aliases>

name_alias_ambiguous.message: Columns {columns} are all aliases of the hydroloom name {name}, and no one of them can be chosen. Drop all but one of them and call again.

placeholders.columns: the input columns that alias the name, comma separated
placeholders.name: the hydroloom name

name_alias_ambiguous.condition: Three or more input columns are aliases of one hydroloom name. When aliases compete, the one earliest in the alias list is set aside: with two, the other takes the name (name_alias_duplicate); with three or more, two or more remain and none can be chosen to carry it.
name_alias_ambiguous.rows: none; the columns are named in the message
name_alias_ambiguous.fix: Drop all but one of the aliasing columns.

column_name_duplicate.condition: Column names are compared lowercased, so two names equal ignoring case collide.
column_name_duplicate.rows: none; the columns are named in the message
column_name_duplicate.fix: Rename one column so the lowercased names differ.
r_text: Names must be unique. <x> These names are duplicated: * "<name>" at locations <i> and <j>.

sf_geometry_name_case.message: The geometry column {column} has uppercase letters, and sf cannot find it once align_names() lowercases the column names. Call hy(x), which keeps the geometry column, instead.
sf_geometry_name_case.condition: On an sf table, sf cannot find the geometry column after its name is lowercased.

sf_mixed_case_names.message: Mixed-case column names on an sf table cannot be renamed by align_names(): sf loses the link between its attribute columns and the geometry. Call hy(x) instead.

nonunique_id_with_toid.message: Non-unique id values detected. This self-referencing table has duplicated rows (likely from divergences). Use to_flownetwork() for a junction-table representation, or make_node_topology() for a fromnode/tonode representation. hy_topo requires unique id.
nonunique_id_with_toid.condition: Divergences gave a flowline more than one row, so hy() returned a flownetwork (one row per downstream connection), not hy_topo, which needs one row per flowline. Functions that take a flownetwork use it as returned; to_flownetwork() is the call for a flownetwork with upmain/downmain set from levelpath.
nonunique_id_with_toid.rows: the rows with a repeated id
nonunique_id_with_toid.fix: make_node_topology(), for one row per flowline connected through the points where flowlines meet (nodes).
r_text: Non-unique id values detected. This self-referencing table has duplicated rows (likely from divergences). Use to_flownetwork() for a junction-table representation, or make_node_topology() for a fromnode/tonode representation. hy_topo requires unique id.

flownetwork_multiple_downmain.condition: A flowline has more than one main downstream path: more than one of its rows has downmain TRUE.
flownetwork_multiple_downmain.rows: the rows with downmain TRUE and a repeated id
flownetwork_multiple_downmain.fix: Correct downmain so each id has one main downstream connection.
r_text: multiple downmain connections per id

flownetwork_multiple_upmain.condition: A flowline receives more than one main upstream path: more than one row pointing to it has upmain TRUE.
flownetwork_multiple_upmain.rows: the rows with upmain TRUE and a repeated toid
flownetwork_multiple_upmain.fix: Correct upmain so each toid has one main upstream connection.
r_text: multiple upmain connections per toid

no_id_column.message: No column was recognized as the identifier id (of each catchment or flowline). Rename the identifier column to id, or register its name as an alias of id.
no_id_column.condition: No input column is id or one of its aliases, so the catchments or flowlines have no identifier. Registering the identifier column's name as an alias of id (hydroloom_names() in R, register_names() in Python) is the alternative to renaming it.
no_id_column.fix: Rename the identifier column to id.
r_text: Unknown or uninitialised column: `id`.

identifier_mixed_type.message: Column {column} holds both text and numbers; an identifier column holds one type. Rows whose type differs from the first value: {rows}. Cast the column to one type and call again.

placeholders.rows: the rows whose value type differs from the first value's

identifier_mixed_type.condition: One identifier column holds both strings and numbers.
identifier_mixed_type.rows: the rows whose type differs from the first value's
identifier_mixed_type.fix: Cast the column to one type before as_hy().

unnamed_name_mapping.condition: The mapping gives hydroloom names without the input column names they apply to.
r_text: input must be named

not_hy_object.condition: The table did not come from hy(), or hy() found flowlines repeated at divergences and returned a flownetwork, whose original names hy_reverse() does not restore.
not_hy_object.fix: Call hy_reverse() on the object hy() returned. For a flownetwork no call restores the original names today.
r_text: must be an hy object

unknown_alias_source.message: source '{source}' is not an alias source in the vocabulary. Pass one of nhdplus, nhdplushr, 3dhp, or hydrofabric.
unknown_alias_source.condition: source is not one of the vocabulary's alias sources. Registering the mapping with register_names() is the alternative to a vocabulary source.
unknown_alias_source.fix: Pass one of nhdplus, nhdplushr, 3dhp, hydrofabric.
